name: Bodo (Central African Republic)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Santandrea, Stefano. 1948. Little known tribes of the Bahr el Ghazal Basin. Sudan Notes and Records 29(1): 78-108; Bodo section '5. A Bantu Tribe: The Bodo', pp. 93-97.
sources.note: Nothing. The Bodo section gives ethnography, a 24-item Bodo/Huma comparative wordlist, a few phrases and possessive paradigms, and one 'phonetical remark' (interchange of b and v: 'the very name of the tribe, usually spelled Bodo, is almost invariably pronounced Vodo'). No word on stress, accent, tone or syllable weight for Bodo (the only accent/tone remark on pp. 93 concerns Biri vs Bviri, not Bodo). Wordlist forms carry no accent marks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page bodo1272 (classification, references) and sister pages homa1239, kari1306
sources.note: Nothing on stress. bodo1272 lists only McMaster 1988 (subclassification, pp. 242, 263) and Campbell et al. 2022 (endangerment); descriptive bibliography = Santandrea 1963 only. homa1239 adds Moseley 2010; kari1306 adds van Bulck 1952, Hackett & van Bulck 1956, Dijkmans 1974 (Kare, a different language).
Nothing; classification D.308 (Maho 2009 NUGL), 15 speakers (Ethnologue 1996 figure), no phonology.

sources.note: The only descriptive work on Bodo (18 pp. covering three Bantu enclave languages of the Bahr el Ghazal/CAR border); Santandrea's outlines of this period normally open with a phonetic paragraph (vowels, consonants, tone/accent), so this is the one place a stress/tone statement for Bodo is likely to exist. Google Books reports 19 pages matching 'Bodo' in the 1963 volume.
